accept: functional tricuspid regurgitation with right heart failure

findings: Right atrial enlargement with tall P waves
Incomplete right bundle branch block pattern

echoTasks.find: Dilated right atrium and right ventricle with a large coaptation gap and tethered leaflets
Dense triangular jet with early peaking on continuous wave Doppler
Dilated inferior vena cava with reduced collapse matching systemic congestion

auscultation.added: Right sided third sound that rises with inspiration
auscultation.murmur: Pansystolic murmur grade 3 of 6 at the left lower sternal edge louder with inspiration

exam.general: Older woman, swollen legs to the knees, ascites with shifting dullness, mild jaundice
exam.jvp: Grossly raised with giant v waves and a brisk y descent
exam.other: Tender hepatomegaly 4 cm, ascites present, basal crackles absent
exam.precordium: Right ventricular heave with a palpable systolic thrill on inspiration
exam.pulse: Regular 88, normal volume, prominent jugular pulsation

history.a: Leg swelling and abdominal fullness for a year, worse by evening, early satiety
Breathless on exertion but can lie flat, no waking gasps
Rheumatic mitral disease treated with valvotomy 20 years ago
No chest pain, no wheeze, passes less urine by day
On diuretics with partial relief, no anticoagulant
Widow living with her son, needs help for clinic visits

keyPoints: Optimise diuresis with loop diuretic plus mineralocorticoid antagonist, watching renal function and potassium
Treat the left sided driver where present and reassess the tricuspid lesion after euvolaemia
Refer to the heart team for tricuspid intervention assessment given systemic congestion
Salt restrict with daily weights and counsel on early reporting of weight gain
Plan dental and skin care to prevent bacteraemia while oedematous and congested
management.model: Aggressive decongestion with driver treatment and heart team referral for tricuspid intervention

sources: ASE guideline on valvular regurgitation, in own words
ESC guideline on valvular heart disease, in own words
stem: A 63 year old woman from Patna, valvotomised for rheumatic mitral disease decades ago, presents with a year of leg swelling, ascites and exertional breathlessness. A pansystolic murmur louder with inspiration, giant jugular v waves, and tense ascites point to systemic venous congestion.
teaching: A murmur louder with inspiration localises regurgitation to the right heart
Severe means orifice 0.40 sq cm or more with vena contracta 7 mm or more
Giant v waves with a dilated cava translate the echo into bedside congestion
Functional disease needs the driver treated and the tricuspid lesion referred together
title: Severe functional tricuspid regurgitation
